label: Cat6a 24-port shielded feed-through patch panel, 1U
description: 1U 19-inch Cat6a shielded feed-through (coupler) patch panel: 24 channels, each an RJ45 on the front and its partner on the rear, rated for 10GBASE-T and PoE++ (802.3bt). Physically passive - a mated front/rear pair is one connector junction, not a repeater - and modelled that way: a frame that arrives on port7 leaves on rear7 and nowhere else.
formFactor: 1U 19-inch, 24 x shielded Cat6a couplers, cable management bar included
notes: FS product 118904 / P/N C6AP-S24FT1U: 'Cat6a Coupler Patch Panel, 24-Port, 1RU', shielded feed-through modules, 'ideal for 10/100/1000Base-T and 10GBase-T Ethernet applications', 10GBase-T and PoE++ rated, cable management bar included; the same family also lists 48-port 2U punch-down variants. Categorised as splitter, matching the passive-panel convention already used for fs/FHD-1U-PP-24LC - there is no dedicated patch-panel category, and inventing one would need a matching palette bucket in web/app.js CAT_ORDER (a category the palette does not know is reachable only by search). What separates a panel from a splitter is not the category but the port pairing: 'pairPrefix' generates rear1-24 and binds each front port to its partner by index, so a frame arriving on port7 leaves on rear7 and on nothing else. Before the engine grew pairs, cabled switch -> port1 then port1 -> host was refused ('d2/port1 is already connected') and a panel was a dead-end patch point; it is now a real two-cable path, and the same change made the existing fibre panel in this catalogue pass traffic rather than terminate it. No MAC table, no flooding, no learning - a mated pair is one junction. Ports carry the full copper ladder (100M-10G) so a panel never silently caps a 10G run.
